A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ExPLAIND research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial additions and reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-reconstruction results, CNN pruning experiments, and Grokking analyses including layer interventions and Lasso regression.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds MNIST validation, EuroLLM checkpoint analysis, causal data-attribution comparisons and checkpoint-subsampling results.

M1.justification: The tensor-accumulation framework remains. v4 refines the published training-feature and atomic-score formulas and adds concrete adaptations: loss-change-ranked checkpoint selection and separate attribution of stored first-moment effects under checkpoint subsampling (Section 4.2, Appendices F.4 and G.2). v2 only proposed general subsampling and early accumulation.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates CIFAR-2 and modulo-113 addition. v4 retains these and adds MNIST digit recognition, multilingual language-model loss analysis using EuroLLM, and counterfactual training-subset prediction evaluations on MNIST and CIFAR-2. These substantially broaden the represented data and task requirements.

E2.justification: The random and Li et al. (2017) pruning comparisons remain in Figure 2. v4 additionally evaluates single-model TRAK and TracIn against ExPLAIND for causal data attribution on MNIST and CIFAR-2 (Appendix G.1, Figure 7); these methods were only cited in v2.

E3.justification: The existing CIFAR-2 and modulo-113 settings remain. New protocols include MNIST training on 5120 samples with 1024 test samples, a separate five-epoch trajectory for subsampling analysis, LDS evaluation using 1000 random training subsets at multiple retention fractions, and simulated single-update EuroLLM evaluations at 37 checkpoints using batches of 3072 sequences of length 4096.

E4.justification: The existing Grokking layer-swapping, reinitialization and cyclic-geometry analyses are retained. v4 adds a sensitivity analysis of reconstruction fidelity versus retained training steps (Appendix G.2, Figure 8) and a EuroLLM case study examining parameter type, layer depth, regularization and first-moment influences (Figures 6, 14 and 15).

E5.justification: Five-run mean and standard-deviation reporting for pruning and Grokking reinitialization remains unchanged. v4 additionally summarizes EuroLLM reconstruction-error variability across checkpoints and displays subsampling error bars in Figure 8 without specifying their statistical meaning or run count. These additions do not establish increased replication of the retained experiments.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 values and Table 2 Lasso coefficients remain unchanged. Added results include MNIST EPK agreement of 0.998/1.0 at 10/100 integration steps, EuroLLM simulated-update reconstruction error averaging 4.46e-8, and CIFAR LDS of 0.06 versus 0.05 for both TRAK and TracIn. New findings concern EuroLLM learning phases, generally stronger MNIST LDS for TRAK except the reported leave-one-out case, and high reconstruction agreement retaining 60% of steps. The aggregate-model heatmaps from v2 Figure 6 are omitted.

T1.justification: v4 substantially revises the AdamW and momentum derivations, introducing weighted batch losses and explicit differentiability assumptions, including the previously omitted stability constant, and keeping time-dependent loss gradients inside the momentum sum. It corrects the parameter summation for regularization, extends Corollary 3.3 to differentiable output functions, and adds detailed composition, activation and partition-accumulation proofs (Appendices F.1-F.4).

C1.justification: The unified-attribution and Grokking-alignment claims remain. v4 expands the principal validation claim to a 1.7B language model and introduces EuroLLM's two-phase pretraining dynamics as a main contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. Attribution across granularities was already claimed in v2.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations connecting EuroLLM's phases to early MLP representation building and later attention-based refinement, and connects first-moment oscillations to unstable local learning dynamics. It also develops substantive qualifications concerning weak counterfactual data attribution, run-specific influences, unavailable example-level momentum attribution at sparse checkpoints, and reconstruction-fidelity versus computation tradeoffs (Section 7, Appendices F.4 and G.1-G.2).

D1.justification: v4 documents the MNIST architecture and optimizer settings, EuroLLM checkpoint and batch construction, approximately 15-minute H100 computations per checkpoint, and subset-retraining and subsampling procedures. Existing model details remain. Code-access documentation becomes inconsistent: Appendix A promises release upon acceptance while the main text retains the GitHub link; v2 explicitly stated that code was available.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds bounded substantive comparisons with DualXDA's input-feature/data attribution and LCA/POLCA's loss attribution. Additional references support MNIST, EuroLLM, Llama and the stability interpretation. The central positioning relative to EPK, TracIn and prior Grokking research remains; numerous publication-metadata updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: v4 updates the abstract, contribution list and conclusion, streamlines theoretical exposition, and edits retained prose. Pruning and efficiency exchange order, while reproducibility and LLM-use statements move to appendices. The overall theory-to-framework-to-case-study organization and much of the original Grokking narrative remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column conference layout. Figure 1 is rearranged and moved to the opening page, Table 1 gains MNIST columns, and Figures 6-8 and 14-15 are added. Existing figures are resized and relocated; v2 Figure 6 becomes v4 Figure 9 with revised labels, a visible color scale and removal of the aggregate Model row.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens mathematical justification and empirical validation. Revised optimizer and loss-gradient derivations repair important weaknesses in v2, while EuroLLM and subsampling experiments test previously speculative scalability. Causal data-attribution comparisons also expose an important applicability limitation. EuroLLM conclusions remain bounded by simulated local updates, and code-release wording is inconsistent, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains in rigor, evidence and clarity about applicability.
